newsitem.title: USA: Xerox Q4 slightly ahead of expectations.
newsitem.headline: Xerox Q4 slightly ahead of expectations.

text.p: Xerox Corp said fourth quarter earnings rose 14 percent to $1.17 per fully diluted share, driven by 26 percent growth in digital products and despite flat sales of its core black and white copiers.
The quarter's $1.17 per fully diluted share compared with Wall Street analysts' consensus expectation of $1.14 per share, according to First Call.
The company, which has refocused its operations in the last year around its document processing operations, also said it planned a series of moves to increase shareholder value.

"The good cash flow from document processing and the expected sales of the Talagen units will enable an acceleration of our stock buyback program this year," Xerox Chairman and Chief Executive Paul Allaire said.
Earlier, Xerox had said it agreed to a deal to sell its Coregis unit, a part of its Talagen insurance subsidiary, to General Electric Co's GE Capital for $450 million.
In addition, Xerox boosted its quarterly dividend to $0.32 per share from $0.29 per share previously.
In February 1996, the board of directors authorized the repurchase of up to $1 billion of Xerox common stock.
By December 31, 1996, the company said it had repurchased 6.5 million shares for $306 million.

The fourth quarter's fully diluted earnings of $1.17 per share compare to 1995's fourth quarter earnings of $1.03 per diluted share, which exclude a tax gain of $0.27 per share and a charge for discontinued operations of $4.73 per share.

Xerox said its revenues grew 8 percent on a pre-currency basis to $5.1 billion in the quarter, driven by 14 percent growth in equipment sales and 41 percent growth in document outsourcing. It said service and rental revenues were essentially unchanged from the fourth quarter of 1995.
Xerox said its operating profit margin improved by 0.5 percentage points, due to an increase in gross margins and a reduction in the ratio of selling, administrative and general expenses to revenues.
The worldwide work force declined by 300 in the quarter to 86,700 as hiring in the company's fast-growing document outsourcing business was more than offset by reductions in other areas.

"Our strategies are driving improved results," Allaire said. "The increase in equipment sales growth is the direct result of our investments in sales coverage and marketing support and excellent customer acceptance of our new digital products."
"The accelerating growth of our digital products and our focus on productivity and expense control are expected to result in continuing earnings growth in 1997."
